title: Order and effort
hook: all is within the hukam, yet the Gurus ask us to strive

segments.voice: Yesterday, Guru Nanak's aarti: the sky as the tray, and the light in everything. Your line: beyond and within. A new week starts.

A farmer in Punjab can't make it rain. She can't choose the heat, or the day the monsoon arrives, or whether a storm flattens the wheat a week before harvest. And still, every season, she's up before light: plowing, sowing, watering, mending the channel where the water runs. Nobody would call her lazy for not controlling the sky, and nobody would call her wise for sitting in the doorway waiting for it. Sikh thought takes her life seriously as a question: if everything happens within God's order, why try?
screen: `SHE CAN'T MAKE IT RAIN.` → `UP BEFORE LIGHT, EVERY SEASON.` → `IF ALL IS ORDERED, WHY TRY?`

segments.voice: Hukam is the Granth's word for the order: the command, the will, the way the One runs everything. In year one you met it as living in tune. In the second pauri of Japji, Guru Nanak says, in paraphrase: by hukam all forms are made; by hukam some are high and some low, some get joy and some get pain. Then the line that leaves no gaps: everyone is within the hukam, and no one is outside it. And yet the same scripture is full of work. Guru Arjan says, in paraphrase: make the effort, and earning by it, live in peace; meditating, you meet the Lord. Sikh life is built on this. Kirat karo, earn an honest living, is one of the pillars Sikhs name beside remembering the Name and sharing. How do the two fit? Sikh teachers say hukam isn't fate in the sense of a script you sit and watch. It's closer to the farmer's sky: the frame you live inside. Your effort is part of the order, not a fight against it. Japji's answer to how to live is, in paraphrase, to walk in the way of the hukam. Walking is still walking; you still lift your feet. That takes a weight off. If everything hung on your effort alone, every failure would be total. If nothing did, there'd be no reason to get up. Within the order, you do your part fully, and let the rest be what it is. Strive within the order.
screen: `HUKAM: NO ONE IS OUTSIDE IT.` · `MAKE THE EFFORT, LIVE IN PEACE.` · `NOT A SCRIPT, A SKY TO WORK UNDER.` · `DO YOUR PART; LET THE REST BE.` · then, large: `STRIVE WITHIN THE ORDER.`

segments.voice: Bring one worry to mind and gently split it in two: the part that's yours, a call, a task, an apology, and the part that isn't, other people's choices, the weather, the outcome. Choose one small piece from your side, and with each out-breath set the other side down.
Order and effort. Everything is within the hukam, and still the Gurus ask for honest work and striving: your effort is part of the order. Today's word.
Your line: strive within the order. The sky isn't yours; the plowing is. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Sikhs recite Japji Sahib, which says all are within the hukam, each morning, and they hold honest work, kirat karo, alongside remembering the Name and sharing as part of daily Sikh life.

chat.says: If everything happens by God's will anyway, why should I bother trying so hard?
options: Your effort is part of the order, Sikh teachers say. Do your part fully; let the rest be.
You shouldn't. Hukam means it's all written, so you just watch it unfold.
Because effort alone decides everything; hukam only covers the weather.
